scope: Automatic runtime context discovery, subscription delivery accounting and interrupted-turn safety. Synthetic content only.
findings: Before repair, a local Responses wire capture contained an unreviewed global AGENTS instruction and the local skills catalog despite the app preview not including them.
A read-only sandbox and a no-shell instruction did not by themselves disable automatic instruction discovery.
project_doc_max_bytes=0 disables project instructions but this pinned runtime still loads global AGENTS instructions independently.
Some model catalog entries select orchestration tools independently of feature flags; disabling a feature does not prove the tool is absent.

Interrupted turns could previously return partial writing as successful output, and usage accounting retained only the last internal response. Requested model aliases were logged without the resolved model.
repairs: Require the verified bundled runtime version before startup; an older or unverified override must not silently ignore privacy controls. The packaging contract must pass when deliberately changing the pin.
Launch and generation use an empty temporary working directory instead of the manuscript directory. Runtime directories are cleaned up on normal exit and startup failure.
The child does not inherit CODEX-prefixed desktop-session variables. Existing dedicated subscription credentials remain in place; no credentials or user configuration were copied or changed.
Disable automatic project instructions, skills instructions, memories, plugins, hooks, connectors and environment access. Explicit host writing instructions replace the default coding instructions.
Read the effective connector names and explicitly disable each before thread creation; an empty configuration table would not remove inherited entries.
Refuse global AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md in the dedicated Codex home before launching or generating, with actionable guidance. Do not delete or rewrite these files.

Keep model-selected orchestration scaffolding restricted to no environments or connector/file tools, disable runtime user-input requests and set one agent slot. The remaining scaffolding is disclosed as a limitation, not represented as a bare text API.
Only a completed turn can produce a usable response. Interrupted, failed, unknown and missing terminal statuses fail closed.

Retain requested and resolved models separately. Use the fresh thread's cumulative reported usage, including reported usage on incomplete turns in rolling budgets. Incomplete turns are not automatically retried.

verification.core: 236 default-suite tests plus the separately executed real-runtime contract, for 237 distinct tests. The wire contract is opt-in in the default suite and required by the macOS packaging gate.
verification.build: Frontend and unsigned macOS app/DMG build passed; packaged Python recovery and the packaged Codex wire contract passed
verification.wire_contract: Real pinned Codex binary connected to a loopback-only synthetic Responses endpoint, with synthetic book instructions, private prose, a skill catalog entry, inherited developer instructions and an unapproved MCP connector. No unreviewed marker, book path, skills catalog or file/connector capability declaration reached the captured request; the connector was not contacted.
verification.failure_contract: Synthetic stdio peer exercised the real subprocess/JSON-RPC bridge through selection generation. Interrupted output created no proposal, left prose unchanged, logged failure and resolved model, and counted 245 reported tokens toward the next request's budget gate.
verification.packaging_gate: scripts/verify_macos_bundle.sh now runs the wire test against the packaged core and packaged Codex binary; make codex-contract-check offers the same check for development

native_live_check.action: Shorten synthetic prose through the native selection preview and generation flow, then reject the result
native_live_check.billing_caveat: Existing subscription quota was used; no API-key billing path was used. This is not a statement that subscription use is free.
native_live_check.outcome: Existing sign-in worked without reauthentication. A reviewable replacement arrived; rejection left the manuscript byte-identical. No suggestion was applied.

limitations_and_next_checks: The subscription runtime still supplies protocol and model-selected orchestration scaffolding. The app preview is explicitly the app-supplied context, not a byte-for-byte preview of the complete provider request.
The empty working directory is not an operating-system sandbox. The wire contract checks the supported pinned configuration, not a compromised runtime or every custom/managed configuration variant.
Exercise forced model tool attempts and profile/managed configuration variants, including proving the no-additional-agent limit under adversarial tool requests.

Abrupt transport loss or local interruption before a usage notification may leave consumed quota unknown. Reported usage is not a hard preflight token cap; subscription max output remains a requested target.
The live test is a delivery/privacy smoke check, not an independent editorial quality benchmark. The prior expansion and critique weaknesses remain unresolved.
Continue safe scene-valid Canon and relationship grounding, full-context limits, other-provider truncation handling and broader native failure testing.
